name: Kam
catalog_citation: Lesage, Jakob. 2020. A grammar and lexicon of Kam (àŋwɔ̀m), a Niger-Congo language of central eastern Nigeria. PhD thesis, INALCO, Paris. https://theses.hal.science/tel-03004919/document
catalog_locator: ch. 4 'Prosodic prominence', §4.1.1-4.1.3 (thesis pp. 95-98); exceptions §4.3.1 Table 32 (p. 110) and §4.3.3 (pp. 112ff.)
catalog_quote: Prosodic strength is specified in the lexicon for every syllable, in a similar fashion that stress can be specified for every stem in some languages, and in a similar way that tonal patterns are also encoded for stems in Kam. ... Prosodic prominence is partly predictable from morphological structure. The first syllable with an onset is usually prosodically prominent in morphological stems, and most morphological stems feature just one prosodic stem. So, the prosodic stem of m̀pīɾī ‘goat’ is pīɾī, the prosodic stem of àlíb ‘head’ is líb, and the prosodic stem of káɾ ‘to accompany’ is simply káɾ. This system is in accordance with what has been found for many other languages in the Macro-Sudan belt (cf. § 1.1), where stem-initial prominence is identified as a salient areal phenomenon ... audit.reasoning: The record rests on the sole and authoritative description of Kam, a 622-page 2020 fieldwork-based reference grammar with a full chapter on prosodic prominence; we hold the PDF and the deciding quotation is verbatim at the cited pages (pp. 96-98, Table 32 p. 110, §4.3.3 p. 112). The classification (lexical prominence with a stem-initial default, pervasive lexical exceptions, no primary/secondary hierarchy, word/prosodic-stem domain) matches the author's own statements ('specified in the lexicon for every syllable'; 'partly predictable.. first syllable with an onset is usually prosodically prominent'; 'many exceptions'). No competing or newer stress/prosody source exists per Glottolog, HAL, ORCID, Crossref, LSP and the thesis's own survey of prior work (wordlists only before 2016). Nothing to add to the list of works to obtain; bibliographic query results
